scope: Pinned source review of simulator warm-up timeout, owned command cleanup, output/reporting semantics and separation from required native/UI acceptance. No numeric CI budget tuning or artifact transport review.

checks.detail: Monotonic work deadline bounds command waits; maximum two attempts and one hosted-CI-only, selected-UDID shutdown recovery. Exit zero observed after deadline is rejected.

Each subprocess starts a new session. Success, nonzero exit, timeout, signal and execution-error paths attempt SIGKILL only against that command's process group and bounded direct-child reaping. Cleanup error/unreaped child is terminal rather than a retry trigger.

Separate stdout/stderr and command receipts retain real return codes, timeout/interruption status and failed attempts. Recovery success is explicitly ready_after_recovery, not a rewrite of the first attempt. Finalization interruption replaces a success receipt.

Warm-up is explicitly continue-on-error diagnostic; the workflow passes steps.simulator_warmup.outcome to test logs rather than interpreting wrapper conclusion as a warm-up pass. Selected xcodebuild retains pipefail, method accounting is required with always(), native Metal methods require one passed occurrence, and finalized xcresult/export checks remain required.

Synthetic tests cover delayed postflight, two timeouts sharing budget, preserved stderr/nonzero status, identity failure, terminal cleanup failure, descendant cleanup after timeout/success/failure, cancellation without recovery, finalization interruption, invalid budgets, existing evidence preservation and late exit zero.

Warm-up command output is file-backed rather than pipe-buffered. No explicit byte ceiling exists for those raw logs, inventory JSON read_text, or host-diagnostic PIPE capture; the host-diagnostic 65536-character slice limits emitted output only after collection. Do not claim a proven memory/disk byte bound from this review.

conclusion: No concrete blocking defect established in the reviewed cleanup/reporting semantics. The source preserves failed preparatory diagnostics separately from genuine selected-test acceptance. No runtime pass or milestone acceptance is established.
